answer: A sybil-resistant agent market can require each identity to earn trust through costly, verifiable work before it can transact at scale. A new agent starts with a small quota, like a lotus bud that must open slowly: it completes audited tasks, and only consistent, honest performance raises its limit. Creating thousands of fake identities then means paying for thousands of separate work histories, while an established agent keeps its quartz-clear record. Colluding newcomers stay in the umber shadows of low trust until they prove themselves, so flooding the market costs more than it can earn.
